title: Crank an empty manual bed's head section to 30-45 degrees and fold the crank away
instruction: Raise the head section of this empty manual bed to between 30 and 45 degrees with its foot-end crank: unfold the handle, turn it clockwise (seen from the robot) until the head section is in that range, then fold the handle back along its shaft and let go.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00, 1,505,900 US workers in 2025; task line "Turn or reposition bedridden patients.") sit a patient up by raising the head of the bed; ATS/IDSA and CDC guidance recommends a 30 to 45 degree semi-upright position against aspiration (Crit Care 2011, bed head elevation review). On a three-crank manual bed such as the Drive Medical 15003P the left foot-end crank raises the head and the cranks fold away when not in use. This trial bed is empty: it tests the crank handling, not a patient's weight. The hard parts, in order: swing the folded handle out 90 degrees past its detent; an 8-turn orbit of the knob on a 140 mm circle against 0.2 N m, the knob spinning in the grip; count the turns (5 degrees each: 6 to 9 are in range, past 12 scores 0); stop at a whole turn so the fold pin is upright, fold the handle back and let go. One hand does it, as for a person; the crank is on the right arm's side.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. The head crank at the foot end of an empty manual bed, modelled on the left crank of a three-crank bed such as the Drive Medical 15003P; sizes are estimates, not measured on that bed. No mattress and no patient. (1) Crank gearbox: fixed grey steel box 90 x 90 x 160 mm standing on the table, x 340 to 430, y -145 to -55, front face at x 340. (2) Crank shaft: 12 mm steel shaft, axis along x at y -100, z 115, projecting 130 mm from the face (tip at x 210). It turns freely against 0.05 N m of bearing friction and drives the head deck through a self-locking worm drive (the deck holds its angle when the crank is let go). Clockwise seen from the robot raises the deck. (3) Crank handle: steel flat 20 x 5 mm, 95 mm long, black, 0.1 kg, pinned at the shaft's tip on a pin perpendicular to the shaft and the flat; 70 mm from the pin to the knob axis. It swings 90 degrees between two stops, held at each end by a spring-ball detent (0.04 N m). Folded (start): the flat lies along the shaft pointing toward the gearbox, tip at x 290. Unfolded: radial, out to the robot's right (-y) when the crank angle is 0. (4) Knob: red nylon cylinder 25 mm across x 70 mm long, 39 g, spinning freely on its pin (0.002 N m), fixed to the flat's end with its axis parallel to the shaft once unfolded; folded, it points along -y, its centre at (280, -145, 115); unfolded, it projects 70 mm toward the robot, its centre at (165, -170, 115) with the crank at 0. Its circle round the shaft is 140 mm across. (5) Head deck: grey steel panel 450 x 550 x 20 mm, 3.0 kg, hinged along y at x 500, z 270 (its lower hinge edge), centred on y -100, flat at the start and resting on a fixed steel frame post 40 x 600 x 260 mm (x 480 to 520). Its angle is 5.0 degrees per net crank turn (raise by turning clockwise seen from the robot, lower anticlockwise); turning forward takes about 0.2 N m (0.05 bearing plus 0.15 for lifting the deck through the worm, about 2.9 N at the knob). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step. Angle: the head deck's angle above flat, 5.0 degrees times net crank turns (forward minus backward turns, never below flat). Folded: the handle's fold angle 15 degrees or less (0 is folded flat along the shaft, 90 is out). Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s every finger zone of both grippers is 30 mm or more from the shaft, the handle and the knob (an unreadable arm counts as not clear), and the deck's angle changes 0.5 degrees or less over that second. Gate: score 0 if at any time the deck's angle exceeds 60.0 degrees (a patient would be folded and sheared). Otherwise: 1.0 angle 30.0 to 45.0 degrees, folded, hands off; 0.5 angle 30.0 to 45.0 degrees but not that whole condition (handle left out, a gripper within 30 mm, or the deck still moving); 0.25 handle folded and the angle from 15.0 up to under 30.0 degrees or over 45.0 up to 60.0 degrees; 0 otherwise (including a deck left near flat). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: angle, a digital inclinometer laid on the head deck (0.2 degrees) or the bed's own gauge; folded, a 15 degree protractor card held against the handle and the shaft; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand and 30 fps video of the last 1 s with the inclinometer in view; the 60 degree gate, the inclinometer's peak hold or a marked 60 degree template at the deck's edge.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Empty bed: a 3 kg 450 x 550 mm deck panel, smaller than a real head section, with no mattress or patient. Sizes, 5.0 degrees a turn and both torques are estimates, not measured on a 15003P, whose cranks fold down under the bed; this handle folds along its shaft. Deck angle is a rule (5.0 degrees per net turn, self-locking); the crank meets 0.05 N m bearing friction plus 0.15 N m while raising. Detents are 0.04 N m joint friction with hard stops.
reset_notes: Lower the head deck to flat by turning the crank anticlockwise (seen from the robot) until the inclinometer on the deck reads 0.0 degrees, then swing the handle back along the shaft until its detent clicks, knob pointing to the robot's right. Nothing is consumed; oil the detent and bearing every 50 trials and check the crank still turns at about 0.2 N m. In the simulator the bed returns to flat with the handle folded.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0; right arm alone: 1.0; left arm alone: 0.0
